target_customer: Women in tech as members; employers paying for access to candidates
problem: Women in tech lacked a safe, harassment free network for advice, jobs and mentorship. Employers paid to reach them.
business_model: Employer subscriptions, TechCrunch reported 20 paying customers at $12,000 per year

founders.name: Cadran Cowansage
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch: YC software engineer from 2016 to early 2019 who created Leap.

founders.name: Kuan Luo
founders.background_notes: Described by Rise as a design leader and retreat architect.

exit.reason: CEO said changes in professional networking and the hiring market made it difficult to sustain Elpha

competitors.name: LinkedIn
competitors.what: General professional network, contrasted by TechCrunch as slow moving

competitors.name: Chief
competitors.funding_then: $3M seed from BBG Ventures then $25M Series A in 2019 per Global Venturing

technical_complexity.rationale: Forum, directory, job board and messaging are standard web features.

defensibility.rationale: A trusted community of 100,000 women created some network effects and employer demand, but features were copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows LinkedIn copying. Elpha shut down in January 2025 citing hiring market changes.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported 20 paying customers including Lambda School and Webflow at $12,000 per year. Elpha reached over 100,000 women by shutdown per Rise.

identity.visual_style: Positioned as a safe space for women in tech
identity.voice_and_tone: Supportive community voice, members called it a lifeline per Rise

branding.brand_signature: Safe, anonymous community for women in tech with a salary database

rebrands.why: Spun out of YC as an independent company, reason for the new name not stated

branding.community_and_virality: Members described Elpha as a lifeline and digital home per Rise (Jan 2025); over 100,000 members

brand_strength.rationale: Strong community identity and loyal members, but no source ties the name itself to growth. Name origin was not found.

outcome_analysis: Elpha began as Leap inside YC, spun out in 2019 with a $1.1M seed and grew to over 100,000 members with employer subscriptions. In January 2025 the CEO said changes in professional networking and the hiring market made it hard to sustain, so it closed. Tech hiring contraction hit its employer revenue, coded macro downturn.
notes: Seed is stated by TechCrunch and Pulse 2.0. Total raised unknown, so earlier funding may be missing. Rise and a search summary call Abadesi Osunsade a co-founder, while another Rise passage calls her first community lead, so she is not listed as founder. elpha.com returned HTTP 503. The Chief date is the year only and Global Venturing page date was not confirmed. The YC batch is Summer 2019, so the Nov 2019 sources fall about three months after Demo Day.
